land.text: the Duchy of Pomerania, a Polish vassal from 1121 whose overlordship 'ended with Bolesław's death' in 1138

predecessors.note: The Duchy of Pomerania page gives 'Established: 1121, as a vassal state of Poland'; Cliopatria draws the duchy from 1139 only, so 1121-1137 sits inside the Kingdom of Poland row (1126-1138).

land.text: the duchy held as a Danish fief after 1185 (Cliopatria draws it inside the Danish realm 1188-1228)

successors.note: Cliopatria row ends with Bogislaw I's death in 1187 and the Kingdom of Denmark shape covers Szczecin from 1188 to 1228 (checked with the gazetteer); the duchy itself did not end, it continued under Bogislaw I's minor sons as a Danish vassal (page infobox 'Denmark (1185-1227)') and then returned to the Holy Roman Empire (1227-1637). A later dossier for the Griffin duchy 1188-1637 is needed.

capitals.name: Stettin (Szczecin)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Stettin (Szczecin)'; no dated list of seats on the page (the first bishopric seat was Wolin, 1140).

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1139 shape applied one year earlier: the duchy became independent when Bolesław III's overlordship ended with his death in 1138

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts 1139, the page has the Polish overlordship ending in 1138. The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison was not possible.

1139-1168, 29,329 km2, bbox 12.78-17.78 E, 52.99-54.82 N: the Griffin duchy from the lower Oder and Szczecin to the Pomeranian coast. The page says 'in 1128, Demmin, the County of Gützkow and Wolgast were already incorporated into Wartislaw I's realm'; no area is given on the page. Eastern edge reaches into Pomerelia (Schlawe-Stolp, which 'Mestwin II of Pomerelia took over' in 1283); soft frontier, within the precision of the era.

correction.text: the 1139 outline, which keeps Demmin and the Gützkow lands west of 13.5 E: Demmin was Duke Casimir I's residence after the 1155 partition, and Henry the Lion besieged it again in 1177

keyframe_review.note: 1169-1176, 26,679 km2: the same duchy without the 12 cells (about 2,650 km2) between Demmin and Tribsees west of 13.5 E that the 1139 shape holds. The page records no territorial change in 1168-1169 (only the 1164 Battle of Verchen, after which 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion', and the 1168 defeat of Rugia), so the trim is Cliopatria's and unexplained; kept as drawn, ledger event at confidence 1. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: verdict was ok and a 1169 loss to holy-roman-empire (confidence 1) bridged the 12-cell trim. The trim is Cliopatria's error; the loss was removed.]

region.text: the Duchy of Pomerania (Szczecin, the Oder mouth and the Pomeranian coast)

ledger.note: 1138: Pomerania becomes independent as Bolesław III dies. Page: 'Polish overlordship ended with Bolesław's death, and Pomerania became independent'; infobox status 'Poland (1121-1138); independent (1138-1160)'; the duchy was established in 1121 as a Polish vassal after Szczecin 'was taken in the winter of 1121-1122'.

1187: Bogislaw I dies and Cliopatria folds Pomerania into the Danish realm. 'Bogislaw I died in 1187, and his sons Casimir II and Bogislaw II were minors'; 'In 1184 and 1185, three campaigns of the Danes resulted in making Bogislaw I, Duke of Pomerania a Danish vassal'; infobox 'Denmark (1185-1227)'. The duchy itself continued; the end here is the end of the Cliopatria row.

wars.name: Battle of Verchen and the Wendish Crusade
wars.outcome: After the 1147 Wendish Crusade and the 1164 Battle of Verchen the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion; no land is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: Saxony has no Cliopatria row before the electorate (1363); the vassal tie is for the Holy Roman Empire or a Saxony dossier to carry.

wars.name: Danish campaigns against Pomerania
wars.outcome: 'Three campaigns of the Danes' in 1184-1185 made Bogislaw I a Danish vassal; Barbarossa had enfeoffed him with the duchy in 1181.
wars.note: No frontier change is recorded; Cliopatria gives the land to Denmark from 1188.

certainty.note: A Slavic duchy between the Oder, the Peene and the Pomeranian coast with no treaty or survey lines on the pages opened; frontiers with Pomerelia, Greater Poland and the Lutician lands are approximate.

notes: eu-15-e. Cliopatria row 'Pomerania' 1139-1187 is the Griffin Duchy of Pomerania (Wikipedia 'Duchy of Pomerania'; the Cliopatria Wikipedia field points to the regional article 'Pomerania', which has no 12th-century dates). Start 1138 follows the page (Polish overlordship ends); the duchy existed since 1121 as a Polish vassal. The end is the end of the Cliopatria row: the duchy continued to 1637 (page infobox: Denmark 1185-1227, Holy Roman Empire again 1227-1637), so a dossier for the Griffin duchy from 1188 is needed (not in Cliopatria after 1187; Cliopatria shows the Danish realm over Szczecin 1188-1228 and the Empire by 1240). Vassal ties of Pomerania (Poland 1121-1138, Saxony 1164-1181, Empire 1181-1185, Denmark 1185-1227) belong to the suzerains' ledgers; no event type records a state as a vassal. The 1155 partition into Pomerania-Demmin and Pomerania-Stettin is internal (one Cliopatria row). Gazetteer: 'Demmin' and 'Tribsees' are not places in the gazetteer (a coordinate radius is used). Pomerelia (Gdansk Pomerania) is not part of this state: the page keeps it under the Samborides as a Polish vassal; the eastern edge of the 1139 shape reaches Schlawe-Stolp. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: the 1169 Demmin-Tribsees trim is not a loss: keyframes 1169 and 1177 now use the 1139 outline and the confidence-1 loss to holy-roman-empire was removed (Demmin was Casimir I's residence; Henry the Lion besieged it in 1177).]
